excerpt: Stop maintaining brittle XPath. Find Selenium elements with plain English, using a 24 MB model that runs locally. No LLM, no API key, no per-call cost. A real run: every element is chosen by the model from the page's own elements. Locators break whenever the front end changes: a renamed class, a moved div, a regenerated id. LLM browser agents can avoid that, but they need an API key, send your pages to a third party, cost money on every step, take seconds per action, and can confidently pick the wrong element. Selenia does one job: it turns a description into an element. A small fine-tuned ranking model scores the real elements on the page against your description and returns the best one. It never writes a selector, so it cannot invent one. If you want an autonomous agent, use an agent. If you want reliable, fast, free locators inside the Selenium tests you already have, use Selenia. pip install selenia Or from source: pip install .from selenium import webdriver from selenia import Selenia driver = webdriver.Chrome() selenia = Selenia(driver) # downloads the model on first use driver.get(" selenia.find("username field").send_keys("standard_user") selenia.find("password field").send_keys("secret_sauce") selenia.find("the login button").click() # Find all matching elements, best match first buttons = selenia.find_all("add to cart button") find returns a normal Selenium WebElement, so it works alongside your existing code, waits and page objects. Elements inside open shadow DOM are found too. More runnable scripts, including a full checkout flow, error handling and a pytest suite, are in examples/. - find raises Selenium's NoSuchElementException when the model is not confident (min_score, default 0.5) or when two elements fit equally well (min_margin, default 0.05).
